item.title: Extreme drought and heat from the last El Niño signal a 'new normal' for tropical forests
item.description:
Waypoint is curating and commenting on third-party reporting. Original publisher: Phys.org.
Summary: During the 2023–2024 El Niño, about 75% of the world's tropical forest areas experienced at least six months of unprecedented simultaneous drought and heat. According to a study published in Earth's Future, this scenario offers more than just a snapshot of an extreme event; it offers a preview of the "new normal" for the next two decades if greenhouse gas emissions are not reduced.
Waypoint’s Take: For someone heading outside, the useful question is observational: watch for phenology cues — bloom, leaf-out, senescence — that mark the season. Keep the publisher’s claims provisional until you read the original. Dashboard conditions can sit beside this report before you leave.
